answer: A marketplace can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before submitting work, then slash it when independent audits verify fraud. Auditors also risk their stake if they make knowingly false claims. A sybil attacker must fund every fake account and leave capital exposed to detection, so multiplying identities raises the cost without multiplying trustworthy reputation. Auditors can trace each thread of evidence through a public pulse of transactions; the marble is not proof of identity, only a marker in that record.
